takes.h: The slipcase is not the film
takes.p: Boutique labels have taught a generation that a horror film arrives in a box with a poster, a booklet and a numbered card. Lovely objects, most of them. But the transfer is the thing you bought. Read the reviews of the disc before the reviews of the packaging.

takes.h: In praise of the bargain box
takes.p: Every convention has one: a long box of paperbacks priced to move, sorted by nobody. It is still the best education this hobby offers, because it forces you to judge a book by its spine, its imprint and its first page, without anyone's listing to tell you what to think.

takes.h: Condition is a description, not a verdict
takes.p: A grade tells you what a copy has been through. It does not tell you whether to want it. Some of the best books on my shelf are reading copies with a cracked spine and a previous owner's name inside the cover. Someone loved them first. That counts for something too.
